::: {.why}
The gap you computed last night is one of the largest and most persistent premia in any market, and this week decides whether that makes it a trade or a warning.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Report the average gap between implied and subsequent realized variance and its distribution over twenty years.
- Say why the premium is compensation rather than mispricing, and what it is compensation for.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Measure it properly in variance rather than volatility: compute implied variance from VIX and realized variance from subsequent daily returns over matching 30-day windows, and report the mean difference, its distribution, and the fraction of months where realized exceeded implied. The mean is positive and the tail is where the losses live.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Say what it pays for: the buyer of variance is buying a payoff that is large exactly when everything else they own is falling, so the premium is an insurance price. Then check that story on your data by reporting the correlation between the variance premium's payoff and equity market returns in the worst months.
:::
:::
